tools.name: get_nearby_events
tools.description:
(MCP tool from rubin-log-insights) Return chronological context around a record_id returned by search_logs.

        Neighbors are ordered by timestamp and record_id. Set same_component to true
        to restrict context to the anchor's component. Temporal proximity is
        evidence of sequence only and does not establish causation.

tools.name: health_check
tools.description: (MCP tool from rubin-log-insights) Confirm that the MCP server is running without querying SereneDB.

tools.name: search_logs
tools.description:
(MCP tool from rubin-log-insights) Search BGL or OpenStack messages with optional filters and match_mode.

        any (default): existing OR-based full-text search, matching any query token.
        phrase: consecutive tokens in order anywhere in the message, using the
        index dictionary's normalization (case/punctuation/spacing may differ).
        exact: equality with the ENTIRE stored raw message, preserving case,
        punctuation, and all whitespace; not a substring or token phrase. Copy a
        returned message verbatim for exact lookup; empty messages are allowed.
        all: every query token must occur, in any order, without adjacency.

        Timestamps must be ISO 8601 values without timezone information. Start is
        inclusive and end is exclusive. Results default to 20 and are capped at 50.
        total_corpus_match_count covers all filtered matches, independently of
        limit. Returns match_mode, executed SQL, bound parameters and truncation.

tools.name: summarize_logs
tools.description:
(MCP tool from rubin-log-insights) Count logs by component, fictional owner team, severity, event_id, or time.

        Use group_by='team' for a LEFT JOIN to the configured fictional ownership map;
        unmatched components remain visible as UNMAPPED. Use group_by='time' with
        interval='hour' or 'day'. Counts cover the complete filtered configured
        corpus; limit only bounds returned groups. Timestamps are naive ISO 8601
        values with inclusive start and exclusive end.

availableModes.name: kiro_guide
availableModes.description: Guide agent that answers questions about Kiro CLI features using documentation

_meta.welcomeMessage:
Welcome to Kiro CLI Guide!

Your friendly AI sidekick, ready to help you get the most out of the CLI. Here's what I can help with:

- Slash commands — /agent, /context, /tools and more
- Built-in tools — read, code, grep... basically superpowers
- Configuration settings — tweak things to your heart's content
- Features — MCP, Code Intelligence, and everything in between
- Create and modify agents, prompts, and configs in ~/.kiro/ and .kiro/

Go ahead, ask me anything about Kiro CLI — no question too weird!

Some fan favorites:
- "How do I save a conversation?"
- "What tools are available?"
- "How does the code tool work?"
- "Create a new agent for me"

Tip: Type /guide again to return to your previous agent
